title: Case Study: EHR Healthcare — Failure Injection & Auto-Healing
purpose: Simulates Healthcare Ransomware Outage & Immutable Backup Recovery: hospital on-premises EMR is encrypted by ransomware; Google Cloud Spanner and GCS immutable backups restore operations.
routing_rationale: Immutable Object Retention policies (Bucket Lock) prevent ransomware from overwriting or deleting historical cloud backups even if administrative credentials are stolen.

nodes.label: Ransomware-Encrypted EMR
nodes.detail: On-premise SAN storage encrypted by malware; hospital clinical staff locked out.

nodes.label: Sever Interconnect Connection
nodes.detail: Network team disables BGP session to prevent ransomware from propagating to cloud.

nodes.label: Locked GCS Backup Vault
nodes.detail: Holds hourly EHR snapshots; immutable retention policy guarantees files cannot be deleted.

nodes.label: Cloud Run Emergency Portal
nodes.detail: Clinicians log into secure Google Cloud portal over BeyondCorp, resuming patient care in 12 minutes.

steps.title: Air-Gap Network Isolation
steps.action: Interconnect severed to protect cloud environment; Cloud Storage Bucket Lock verified intact.
steps.why_traversal: WORM (Write Once, Read Many) compliance prevents ransomware from tampering with cloud backups.

steps.title: Emergency Cloud Activation
steps.action: Emergency clinical portal activated; doctors access patient medical records securely.
steps.why_traversal: Restores life-saving clinical operations without paying ransom.

scenarios.label: Attacker Tries to Delete Immutable Backups
scenarios.root_cause: Attacker obtained GCP Project Owner credentials and ran 'gsutil rm -r gs://ehr-backups'.
scenarios.diverted_path: Cloud Storage Bucket Lock strictly rejects deletion: retention policy active.
scenarios.recovery: Revoke compromised admin credentials and notify enterprise incident response team.
